records.text: In Swedish, 'morfar' literally means mother's father and 'farfar' means father's father; a Swedish grandfather would not permit a grandchild to use the wrong term.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #1 (Ep ZAsV0fHGBiM)

appearances.snippet: Now I'm paraphrasing, but they said Candace, ... Morfar quite literally translates into mother's father. ... And farfar quite literally translates into father's father. ... no Swedish grandfather would ever allow you to refer to him as Morfar if he was not actually your Morfar,

verification.notes: Swedish dictionaries distinguish morfar as maternal grandfather and farfar as paternal grandfather. The added cultural claim that a Swedish grandfather would never permit misuse of the term is an unsupported absolute, so only the linguistic portion is verified.

records.text: You see, I received a flurry of emails from our fans in Sweden about this particular post and they did not like this post.
records.speaker: Candace Owens
